items.title: Plain-language program map (wiki) anchored to palace nodes
Chorus portents: foreboding when work goes back on its requirements (again)
items.description: Kohl, 2026-10-15: the Chorus (PR #59, the audience-reception agent) should give ominous portents of doom when a piece or a plan goes back on its requirements again, the tragic chorus watching the hero walk toward what everyone can see coming. Needs memory, since 'again' is the point: compare the piece against its stated requirements (an edict's acceptance criteria, a ticket, what the author said they were building) and against earlier reversals (edict amendments, earlier reception reports, dropped proposals, epitaphs). Stays reception, not verdict: the Chorus says how it lands and what it dreads; Momus checks whether it's wrong. Also: keep the name Hermes free for inter-agent communication (the board, edict 0009).

items.title: Edicts with tests attached
items.description:
Built: PR #56 (merged): `daedalus edict tests`.

From a dream (speculative): `daedalus dream show 2026-10-15`.

**Edicts with tests attached** (from i38). This is the one tonight's work pointed at. Most of building 0011 was translating acceptance criteria into tests one by one, by hand, and checking that each criterion had one. *What would make it real:* an `Acceptance criteria` section in a lightly structured form (a bullet per criterion, with a stable id). An `edict accept` hook would generate `tests/edicts/test_NNNN.py` with one skipped, named test per criterion. Doctor would then flag criteria whose test is still skipped. Kohl still writes the criteria, and Daedalus fills in the bodies. "Is edict 0011 built?" becomes a test run.

items.title: The TUI speaks Ophanic, in both directions
items.description:
In review: PR #71 (stacked on #70): TUI send form, Ophanic snapshots + A/B log.

From a dream (speculative): `daedalus dream show 2026-10-15`.

**The TUI speaks Ophanic, in both directions** (from i12 and i11). The thesis says text grids are what the model reads best, and the TUI design is already 48 `.oph` diagrams. Make "Send to Claude" send the focused panel as an Ophanic snapshot, and test whether Claude's answers about the dashboard are better than with a prose dump: that's a small, falsifiable experiment on the thesis, run inside Daedalus. *What would make it real:* a renderer from panel state to `.oph` (the widgets already correspond to `◆` components, per edict 0012). Then an A/B harness, like reflection's, that logs which form the session got and whether the next action was right. The reverse direction (render the TUI *from* the diagrams) can wait until the first half shows a difference.

items.title: Intake from the codebase's own pain
items.description:
Built in PR #64 (open, for Kohl's review): the `self` source.

From a dream (speculative): `daedalus dream show 2026-10-15`.

**Intake from the codebase's own pain** (from i23). Sources made intake pluggable tonight. The most honest tracker Daedalus has access to is itself: reflection's digests already count retries and failures, Theseus scores complexity, and doctor finds drift. *What would make it real:* a first-party `self` source whose `fetch()` reads those local files. That's no network and no new permissions, just one more plugin through the seam that shipped tonight. Its items are labelled as Daedalus's observations, and land as proposals like everything else. It also gives aspirations (18) a principled home: aspirations as a second kind from the same source, entropy marked as entropy.

items.title: The state-of-the-project page
items.description:
Built: PR #57 (merged): `daedalus page`.

From a dream (speculative): `daedalus dream show 2026-10-15`.

**The state-of-the-project page** (from i33). The TUI's goal is legibility for someone who wasn't there, but that someone has to install it first. A published, read-only page generated at exhale would do half the TUI's job for zero install: the active phase, the edicts and their status, what needs whom, and the last session in plain words. *What would make it real:* the exhale skill gains a step that renders the gameplan and edicts to one HTML page from the same library functions the TUI uses (one source of truth, edict 0012's rule), and republishes it to a stable URL. Kohl decides whether it's shared.

items.title: The roadmap remembers why things died
items.description:
Built: PR #58 (merged): epitaphs.

From a dream (speculative): `daedalus dream show 2026-10-15`.

**The roadmap remembers why things died** (from i14). Tonight I made a dropped update move the baseline, so it doesn't come back. That's right for the sync, but it erases the signal that someone keeps asking for something. *What would make it real:* an `epitaph` on dropped and closed-unbuilt items, and a doctor hint when the same external id or a near-duplicate title is dropped a third time. It's small, and it's the kind of pattern only a system that keeps everything can notice.
